Codex can also answer questions or update the PR. Try commenting "@codex address that feedback".

**18 issues found** across 125 files

**Note:** This PR contains a large number of files. cubic only reviews up to 75 files per PR, so some files may not have been reviewed.

<details>
<summary>Prompt for AI agents (unresolved issues)</summary>

```text

Check if these issues are valid — if so, understand the root cause of each and fix them. If appropriate, use sub-agents to investigate and fix each issue separately.


<file name="datafn/examples/apple-webview-host/DatafnAppleHost/App/ContentView.swift">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/examples/apple-webview-host/DatafnAppleHost/App/ContentView.swift:123">
P2: Topology switches start uncancelled concurrent activation tasks, so rapid changes can race and apply stale runtime state from an older selection.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnWebViewBridgeHost/DatafnWKWebViewBridgeHost.swift">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnWebViewBridgeHost/DatafnWKWebViewBridgeHost.swift:107">
P1: `evaluateJavaScript` is called off the main thread. After the `await` on `dispatcher.dispatch`, the unstructured `Task` can resume on any executor, but `WKWebView.evaluateJavaScript` must run on the main thread. The event-delivery path correctly uses `Task { @MainActor … }` — this response-delivery path should do the same.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/swift-bridge/README.md">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/swift-bridge/README.md:5">
P3: The `What It Exports` list is incomplete: `createNativeBackedSearchProvider(...)` is exported by the package but missing from this section.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnAppleRuntime/DatafnAppleRuntime.swift">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnAppleRuntime/DatafnAppleRuntime.swift:264">
P3: `started` is written but never read. Unlike `DatafnServerSyncEngine` which guards on `started`, this actor never checks it — `start()` can be called multiple times, re-starting sync engines without protection.</violation>

<violation number="2" location="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnAppleRuntime/DatafnAppleRuntime.swift:266">
P2: The two `init` methods duplicate ~30 lines of identical property assignments. If a new property is added or wiring changes, both must be updated in lockstep. Consider extracting the shared assignment into a helper or having the public init delegate to the internal one with a `nil` monitor.</violation>

<violation number="3" location="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnAppleRuntime/DatafnAppleRuntime.swift:634">
P1: The `databaseScope` is hardcoded to `.privateDatabase` instead of forwarding `cloudKit.databaseScope`. The sync engine and snapshot both use the user's configured scope, but the Core Data store ignores it. If a non-private scope is ever configured, the store and sync engine will disagree on which CloudKit database to use.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnServerSync/DatafnServerSyncEngine.swift">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnServerSync/DatafnServerSyncEngine.swift:82">
P1: `started` is set to `true` before the async work that can throw. If `cloneNow()` or `pullNow()` fails, `started` stays `true` and future `start()` calls silently return, making the engine unrecoverable without explicitly calling `stop()` first. Reset `started` in the error path so the caller can retry.</violation>

<violation number="2" location="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnServerSync/DatafnServerSyncEngine.swift:168">
P2: `cloneNow()` and `reconcileNow()` lack the in-flight reentrancy guards that `pullNow()` and `schedulePush()` use. Due to Swift actor reentrancy, concurrent calls can enter these methods when the actor suspends at `await`, potentially running duplicate clone/reconcile operations against the store.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/client/src/query.ts">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/client/src/query.ts:168">
P2: Enforce the iCloud remote-only resource restriction for batch queries too. The current check is only in the single-query path, which allows `client.query([...])` to bypass the unsupported-resource guard.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/swift-bridge/src/nativeSearchProvider.ts">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/swift-bridge/src/nativeSearchProvider.ts:105">
P2: Guard against undefined searchFields before calling .map; otherwise configs that omit searchFields crash at runtime.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnCoreDataStore/CoreDataModelBuilder.swift">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnCoreDataStore/CoreDataModelBuilder.swift:191">
P2: Case-insensitive entity name collision is not caught by validation. `sanitize()` lowercases all characters, so resources named e.g. "Foo" and "foo" both map to entity name `df_record_foo`. But `validate()` uses a case-sensitive `Set`, so it won't detect the duplicate — leading to a Core Data model conflict at runtime.</violation>

<violation number="2" location="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnCoreDataStore/CoreDataModelBuilder.swift:518">
P1: The `indexed` parameter is silently discarded (`indexed _: Bool`). Every call site that passes `indexed: true` has no effect — no index is ever created on the Core Data attribute. This will degrade query performance for all indexed lookups (id, key, resourceName, namespace, etc.).

The `_` as an internal name means the value is never bound. Either use `NSFetchIndexDescription` on the entity or, for older APIs, set the property on the attribute.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnWebViewBridgeHost/DatafnBridgeDispatcher.swift">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnWebViewBridgeHost/DatafnBridgeDispatcher.swift:753">
P1: Remote profile validation is bypassed when the client omits `remoteProfile`. If `configuration.remoteProfile` is set (e.g. `"production"`), a client that sends no `remoteProfile` field passes all three optional bindings' short-circuit and completes the handshake without matching the expected profile. Guard on the server-side expectation first, then compare.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/swift-bridge/src/wkwebviewBus.ts">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/swift-bridge/src/wkwebviewBus.ts:99">
P2: Handle synchronous `postMessage` errors so callers still receive a bridge error response and the pending request is cleaned up.</violation>
</file>

<file name="searchfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started-swift.mdx">

<violation number="1" location="searchfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started-swift.mdx:93">
P2: This link targets a missing docs route (`/docs/reference/adapters`), so readers hit a dead end from the new Getting Started page.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnCoreDataStore/DatafnCoreDataStore.swift">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/swift/Sources/DatafnCoreDataStore/DatafnCoreDataStore.swift:945">
P1: The `healthChangedEvent` constructed inside `setSearchMetadata` is silently discarded (`_ = try performMutatingOperation`). Every other mutating method captures and `emit()`s the event. Observers (including the SwiftUI layer and the WebView bridge) will never learn about search-metadata status changes.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/client/src/mutate.ts">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/client/src/mutate.ts:422">
P1: Don’t let push scheduling errors fail `mutate()` after the local mutation is already committed. Handle `schedulePush()` fail-soft here so callers don’t retry and duplicate/conflict with already-persisted mutations.</violation>
</file>

<file name="datafn/swift-bridge/package.json">

<violation number="1" location="datafn/swift-bridge/package.json:8">
P1: Exporting `./src/index.ts` as the runtime entrypoint makes this package source-only; publish/consume paths should point to built JS (with `.d.ts` types) like the other DataFn packages.</violation>
</file>
```

searchfn/swift/Sources/SearchFnCore/SearchFnResourceEngine.swift-188-199 (1)
